name: DLF Ltd
about: DLF Ltd with its subsidiaries, associates and JVs is engaged in real estate development, from the identification and acquisition of land to planning, execution, construction and marketing of projects. It is also engaged in business of leasing, generation of power, provision of maintenance services, hospitality and recreational services which are related to the overall development of real estate business. [1]

sections.one_liner: Luxury Gurugram developer with a rental JV. Its core P&L is shrinking while it waits on an FY27-28 completion-led revenue inflection.
business: Develops luxury and super-luxury housing, mainly in Gurugram. FY26 bookings were Rs 20,143cr, 2.5x reported FY26 revenue of Rs 8,194cr. [AR FY26]
Rental arm DCCDL has a ~50msf office/retail portfolio at 96% area and 97% value occupancy. Q2 revenue Rs 2,014cr, PAT Rs 750cr. [Q2FY27 call]
Hospitality: 2 hotels plus clubs, Rs 626cr FY26 revenue (6%). The AR's 75% annuity share conflicts with DCCDL being a JV, so the true mix is unclear. [AR FY26]
Recognises revenue only on project completion. Rs 75,000cr of launched projects reach the P&L from FY27-28. [Q2FY27 call]
financial_snapshot: Q2FY27: revenue Rs 1,261cr (-23% YoY), EBITDA Rs 23cr (1.8% margin), PAT Rs 1,301cr (+10%). PAT is 57x EBITDA. [Numbers]
TTM: revenue Rs 6,375cr, EBITDA Rs 974cr (15.3% margin), PAT Rs 4,567cr. Core operations contribute about a fifth of profit. [Numbers]
Valuation: market cap Rs 1,70,401cr. P/E 37.1x, P/B 3.7x, about 27x TTM revenue. [Numbers]
Returns on a Rs 45,587cr equity base are low: ROCE 6.3%, ROE 9.5%. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue grew 12.9% a year over 3 years, but H1FY27 revenue of Rs 2,541cr is down 42% YoY. [Numbers]
PAT grew 29.5% a year over 3 years, more than twice revenue growth. EBITDA fell from Rs 2,124cr (FY24) to Rs 1,449cr (FY26). [Numbers]
Operating margin compressed from 33% (FY24) to 18% (FY26), then 12% and 1.8% in the last two quarters. [Numbers]
ROCE has stayed at 4-7% for six years despite PAT quadrupling. Profit growth is not lifting capital returns. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings fell from Rs 4,834cr (FY24) to Rs 314cr (Sep-26). D/E is 0.01. [Numbers]
Net cash is Rs 15,100cr, about 9% of market cap, after a Rs 1,980cr dividend. [Q2FY27 call]
Working-capital days fell from 788 to 245 over FY21-26. Much cash sits in RERA accounts (Rs 10,400cr) and unlocks over FY27-28. [Numbers] [Q3FY26 call]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT averaged 1.23x over 3 years. FY26 CFO of Rs 6,347cr was 1.44x PAT. [Numbers]
FCF rose from Rs 2,321cr (FY23) to Rs 6,231cr (FY26), a 39% CAGR, driven by customer advances, not P&L profit. [Numbers]
H1FY27 operating cash flow is about Rs 3,158cr (Rs 1,300cr + Rs 1,858cr). That annualises to ~Rs 6,300cr, below the Rs 7,000-8,000cr guide. [Q1FY27 call] [Q2FY27 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management cites Q2 revenue of Rs 2,298cr and EBITDA of Rs 1,060cr. Screener shows Rs 1,261cr and Rs 23cr. The gap includes a Rs 738cr one-time gain. [Q2FY27 call] [Numbers]
Management cites FY26 revenue of Rs 10,000cr at a 46% gross margin. Reported revenue is Rs 8,194cr with an 18% operating margin, down from 33%. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
The 'strong profitability' story depends on below-EBITDA items. FY26 PAT of Rs 4,415cr was 3x EBITDA of Rs 1,449cr. [Numbers]
The cash story checks out. Debt fell Rs 3,797cr in FY26, matching the 'zero gross debt' claim. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]
guidance: FY27 sales bookings of Rs 20,000cr, about Rs 9,000cr of new margin a year. Reiterated in August despite Goa being excluded. [Q4FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
Development portfolio gross margin potential is ~Rs 40,000cr and cash potential Rs 42,500cr. Revenue inflection expected FY27-28 as Arbour completes. [Q2FY27 call]
Rental targets keep changing basis: Rs 7,400-7,500cr (Jan), Rs 8,200cr (May), then a Rs 7,300-7,500cr exit rate (Aug). [Q3FY26 call] [Q4FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
DevCo free cash flow guided at Rs 7,000-8,000cr a year, with dividends to grow. The dividend stays annual. [Q4FY26 call] [Q2FY27 call]
Medium-term rental NOI growth guided at mid-teens, with 20-25% revenue CAGR over 4-5 years. [Q4FY26 call]

ledger.promised: Kolkata IT SEZ sale to close, with full recognition in Q4. [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: AR shows a Rs 489cr IT Park sale gain. Q4 PAT was Rs 1,269cr, -1% YoY.
Collections Rs 13,500cr (+15%). CFO Rs 6,347cr, up 21% YoY.

ledger.promised: Arbour 2 senior living, ~Rs 2,000cr GDV, to launch in Q4FY26. [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Launched in Q2FY27 as Aureva, Rs 1,900cr booked. Two quarters late; Q1FY27 bookings were only Rs 657cr.

ledger.promised: Dividend payout to continue at 75-80% of PAT. [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Rs 8/share, about Rs 1,980cr, is 45% of consolidated PAT of Rs 4,415cr.

ledger.promised: Sales bookings of Rs 20,000cr. [Q4FY26 call, reiterated Q1FY27]
ledger.delivered: H1: Rs 4,457cr, 22% of target. H2 needs ~Rs 15,500cr.
Q2 non-Aureva bookings are at most ~Rs 1,900cr. H1 Dahlias is capped at ~Rs 2,557cr.

ledger.promised: DevCo FCF of Rs 7,000-8,000cr a year. [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: H1 operating cash flow ~Rs 3,158cr, annualising to ~Rs 6,300cr. FY26 FCF was Rs 6,231cr.

ledger.promised: Revenue inflection as Arbour hits the P&L. [Q1FY27 call; restated FY27-28 in Q2FY27]
ledger.delivered: Not yet visible: Q1 revenue -52.9% YoY, Q2 -23.3% YoY.

bull: Rs 40,000cr development gross margin potential is about 23% of market cap, and is backed by Rs 20,143cr of FY26 bookings. [Q2FY27 call] [Q4FY26 call]
Net cash of Rs 15,100cr, with Rs 10,400cr of RERA cash unlocking in FY27-28. Funds a rising dividend and land buying without debt. [Q2FY27 call] [Q3FY26 call]
Pricing is strong: Dahlias prices up 10%, units at Rs 120-125cr, Aureva sold out. DCCDL PAT is growing 17-20% YoY. [Q2FY27 call] [Q1FY27 call]
bear: Core EBITDA of Rs 23cr in Q2 (1.8% margin). A 37x P/E rests on JV and one-off income, with ROE at 9.5%. [Numbers]
FY27 bookings are 22% of the Rs 20,000cr guide at half-year. Q3 faces 30-40 days of GRAP construction halts. [Q2FY27 call]
Management's figures run above reported ones (FY26 revenue Rs 10,000cr vs Rs 8,194cr), and the rental guidance basis keeps changing. Hard to hold them accountable. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
questions: What is the Q2 core EBITDA excluding the Rs 738cr gain and other income?
Which H2 launches deliver the remaining ~Rs 15,500cr of FY27 bookings?
Why did DLF's own rental run-rate fall from Rs 1,150cr to Rs 750cr?
Is the 75-80% dividend payout measured on standalone or consolidated PAT?

themes: Strong demand for luxury and super-luxury residential with sellouts and price momentum

Dahlias pricing algorithm driving consistent increases; North premium over South INR 20-25 crores

Strong cash generation enabling higher dividends while maintaining INR 15,100 crores net cash
Regulatory dependency on approvals; GRAP air quality restrictions may impact Q3 construction

Revenue shortfall vs expectations: Why below market despite good launches? Management: Completed-contract accounting; inflection FY27-28

analyst_pushback.pushback: Why stuck at INR 200-220bn when peers at INR 300-350bn?
analyst_pushback.response: Presales is wrongest metric. We chase margins and cash flows, not volume. INR 9-10k crores margin annually is priority.

analyst_pushback.pushback: Price per sq ft differential vs Camellias on super carpet basis?
analyst_pushback.response: Dahlias caught up in 1.5 years vs expected 4 years. Now near parity with Camellias; significant headroom ahead.

analyst_pushback.issue: RERA cash deployment with INR 14tn balance
analyst_pushback.pushback: What's the plan when INR 11.2tn RERA balance unlocks FY27-28?
analyst_pushback.response: Three-pronged: increase shareholder returns, invest in pipeline capex, pursue margin-accretive opportunistic deals.

analyst_pushback.pushback: How will CCM accounting method affect P&L given project completions?
analyst_pushback.response: Virtuous cycle: Arbour, other projects deliver FY27-28 onwards, boosting margins and FCF despite conservative accounting.

annual_report.business: Real estate developer and operator. Develops and sells premium residential (high-rise, low-rise, plotted), mixed-use properties for HNI customers and institutional investors. Operates ~50msf rental portfolio (offices, retail at 95% occupancy) for corporate tenants. Operates hotels and clubs. Revenue: property sales, rental income, hospitality services.
annual_report.revenue_mix: Geographies: Gurugram (primary), Mumbai, Delhi-NCR, Chennai, Hyderabad. Products: Premium residential (42% launches >₹1.5cr), commercial offices, retail malls. Customers: HNI individuals, multinational corporates, retail brands.
strategy: Premium product positioning, execution excellence, disciplined capital allocation
Rental platform expansion targeting ₹10,000cr revenue medium-term
Development pipeline monetization (₹1.14 lakh cr identified potential)
Balance sheet strengthening, zero gross debt in development achieved
annual_report.outlook: Residential market constructive, premium/luxury segments healthy. Office sector in record upturn. Retail showing strong momentum. Development business expected strong cash generation. Target: rental revenue surpasses ₹10,000cr medium-term.
annual_report.capex_plans: ~27msf under execution, ~25msf launch pipeline, ~137msf residual development potential. ~2.7msf retail pipeline. ~0.37msf average annual new retail additions.
risks: Macro-economic: inflation, interest rate volatility, geopolitical tensions (West Asia conflict)
Regulatory: changes in development guidelines, environmental clearances, taxation frameworks
Operational: execution delays, supply chain disruptions, cyber security threats
Market: customer sentiment fluctuations due to external factors, competition
annual_report.flags: Promoter: Rajdhani Investments (61.53%). Exceptional items: ₹489cr IT Park sale gain. Merger of DLF Urban into DLF Home Developers. Asset divestment ₹710.23cr. No auditor qualifications noted.
